profile_headline: Course Lead in Artificial Intelligence at UC Berkeley
post_content:
Google Brain just published an insightful paper on data parallelism and batch
size in neural networks: Measuring the Effects of Data Parallelism on Neural
Network Training. \- authors focus on synchronous SGD \- goal of the paper is
simple: "we attempt to provide the most rigorous and extensive experimental
study on the effects of data parallelism on neural network training to date"
\- "Some authors contend that large-scale data parallelism is harmful in a
variety of ways, while others contend that it is beneficial" \- this is very
interesting: "We show that the relationship between batch size and number of
training steps to reach a goal out-of-sample error has the same characteristic
form across six different families of neural network, three training
algorithms, and seven datasets." \- another noteworthy claim: "SGD with
momentum (as well as Nesterov momentum) can make use of much larger batch
sizes than plain SGD" \- authors didn't find simple relationships between the
optimal value of hyperparameters (e.g. learning rate) and batch size \-
authors didn't see decreased performance with larger minibatches but
additional regularization techniques may be needed https://lnkd.in/fXB8eJ8
